stem: A 4-year-old boy has been struck by a van at about 50 kph. He is tachypnoeic, has reduced air entry on the left, and asymmetric chest movement. Which additional bedside finding would most help you decide the next step in management?
explanation: In a trauma primary survey, the key bedside information is whether the reduced air entry is associated with hyperresonance or dullness, which helps distinguish pneumothorax from haemothorax and guides urgent management.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 1 - Primary survey

rationale: The scenario suggests a serious thoracic injury during ABC assessment. Percussion note is the most useful additional bedside finding among the options.

optionExplanations.A: Not a routine or practical assessment in acute paediatric trauma primary survey.
optionExplanations.B: May provide oxygenation/ventilation data, but is not the most immediately helpful bedside discriminator here.
optionExplanations.C: Helps differentiate hyperresonance (pneumothorax) from dullness (haemothorax/contusion) and informs urgent next steps.
optionExplanations.D: Relevant to asthma/airflow obstruction, not acute chest trauma assessment.

source.quizTitle: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 1 - Primary survey
source.questionTextHtml:
Currently James is breathing at a rate of 50 breaths per minute, with his right side apparently moving more than his left. There are a few bruises over the anterior left chest but no obvious wounds or deformities. There is poor air entry on the left side compared to the right. Oxygen saturations are 98% in high flow oxygen (88% in air), heart rate 120bpm and conscious level remains decreased. At this stage, there is suggestion of a serious breathing problem to address before moving on.

Which one of the following pieces of additional information would be helpful in deciding the next steps?

Clinical scenario 1 - James

Teaching/learning points:

Initial ABC approach to trauma patient

Recognition of life-threatening injury and resuscitation priorities

You receive a pre-hospital alert from paramedics regarding James, a four year-old boy who ran away from his mother onto the road, where he was hit by a van at approximately 50kph. He hit the windscreen and was thrown approximately 7 metres. He was unconscious at the scene and not moving spontaneously. The paramedic crew on the scene report him to be unconscious but breathing, with a respiratory rate of 30/min, heart rate 120bpm, multiple abrasions and bruises. ETA 10 minutes.

The following 12 questions refer to James' clinical scenario.
